_meta.note: Second pass over the GPT-6 Astra system card after an audit found the S260 pass had only mined the capability sections (§10.1.2 cyber, §10.1.3 AI self-improvement, §6.1 HealthBench). This batch adds the safety/robustness/bio-critical tables that were missed: Table 1 (production disallowed content), Table 2 (U18), Table 3 (agentic safe completion), Table 4 (image input), Table 5 (static jailbreak, with 95% CIs), Table 7 (dynamic adversarial simulations), Table 8 (harmful outcomes in work environments), §10.1.1 bio High + CRITICAL evaluations (Tables 12-17), SecureBio external evaluation, §5.2 prompt injection + Gray Swan IPI, Table 20 (cyber safety), Table 21 (Daybreak Blue), and §8.6 Codex deployment-simulation misalignment flags. Every value was read from a local `pdftotext -layout` extraction. Existing benchmark ids were reused wherever GPT-5.6 Sol or earlier GPT-5.x models already had rows (verified by matching comparator values against the DB); new ids created only where none existed. Where this card restates a Sol baseline that differs from the DB's existing Sol row (HPCT 66.5 vs 68.4, WCB 67.6 vs 68.3, ReproBAIT 69 vs 85, gore 0.785 vs 0.708, sexual 0.915 vs 0.948), the existing row was LEFT ALONE and the discrepancy recorded in notes — OpenAI states scores across system cards are not directly comparable. NOT INGESTED (figure-only or non-triple): Figures 1-6 (safety Pareto, multiturn jailbreak defender success by attacker budget, hallucination rates on user-flagged conversations), §8.7 metagaming/alignment faking rates, §8.8 UK AISI + Apollo Research eval-awareness percentages, §9 monitorability/CoT controllability and monitor-recall percentages, §10.1.3 KernelGen/PostTrainBench/MLE-Bench (charts only), Figure 41 no-CoT time horizon. CORRECTION during this same pass: an initially-declared new id 'dna_sequence_design_tf_binding_pass1' duplicated the existing 'dna_tf_binding_design_pass1' (same Nucleobench/Ledidi eval, identical comparator values) — dropped, Astra's 11.27 re-filed onto the existing id, and the three duplicate comparator rows removed since the DB already had them. All other new ids were fuzzy-matched against the full benchmark table and confirmed distinct.
